stage1.impression: A clean, competent CG product shot rather than a photograph of a bar: one red translucent speaker on a pale plinth caught in a hard theatrical spotlight pool, beside a warm concrete wall, an orange leather chair and a dark record wall. The concrete is the most convincing surface; the speaker's acrylic reads salmon-pink and overlit, more like a lit display piece or plastic than thick cast acrylic, and the floor pool and wall hotspot make it a showroom, not a cozy night room. No beams, no props, no sign of life.

blocking_9: The floor pool under the speaker must stop reading as a stage spot: region [130,380,360,440] lum_median below 140 with a soft edge, not a hard ellipse
The wall right of the speaker must not be the brightest surface in the frame: [365,180,470,380] lum_median below 130

The Ember acrylic must read as deep, thick tinted acrylic (red dense in the body, glowing at polished edges), not washed pink: speaker [210,180,365,395] r_median/g_median ratio of 2 or more and lum_p95 below 190
Only one saturated colour: the leather chair must drop back to a dark, desaturated tan or black so the speaker is the only red-orange in frame
Fir beams or ceiling and at least one lived-in prop (a glass, a record out of its sleeve, a coat on the chair) visible, so it reads as a listening room in use rather than a product on a plinth
Practicals coherent and warm: the sconce currently renders near white, it should read as a 2400 K amber lamp

defects.what: Hard-edged, near-white spotlight ellipse on the floor (median 200, 2% clipped); falls from ~196 to ~54 in one profile bin. Reads as a stage spot or a showroom.
Concrete beside and behind the speaker blown to a hot, almost neutral white wash (median 197), brighter than the speaker itself.
Speaker acrylic overlit and pastel: salmon-pink panels with flat fill, interior parts read as pink plastic; the tint lacks depth and the edges do not glow more than the faces.
Specular streak on the top panel is a small, smeared, plastic-looking highlight; the panel reads as soft and slightly wobbly rather than crisp polished acrylic.
Leather lounge chair is a saturated orange-red that competes with the Ember tint; its surface is smooth and CG, with no creasing or grain at 1:1.
Sconce shade renders cool white (5% clipped) rather than 2400 K amber; the lamp looks like a neutral LED fitting.
Record wall and cabinet are mostly dark and slightly soft (median 23-25); sleeves read as vertical colour streaks, not individual spines; no highlights on records.
Pale timber plinth is bright and close to raw pine, reading as unfinished; it pulls the eye down to the hotspot.
Overall image is soft with denoiser smoothing on concrete and timber at 1:1; no haze visible in the beams of light; frame is empty of props.
No ceiling or fir beams in frame despite the card's brief; low, level camera crops them out.

changes.problem: The pendant spot over the speaker makes a hard, near-white pool on the floor and a hot wash on the wall, turning the frame into a showroom.

evidence.measured: lum_median 200.3, clip 2.0%; wall [365,180,470,380] median 197.5; profile y drops 196 to 54 across one bin

change.setting: pendants 3 x spot, 60.0 W, cone 50.0 deg
change.to: 25 W, cone 70 deg with blend about 0.6 (soft edge), aimed so the pool falls on the floor in front of the chair rather than on the wall behind the speaker

changes.expected: A warm, soft pool that falls off gradually, the wall behind the speaker dropping into mid-tone, and frame median falling toward 45.

changes.problem: The Ember speaker is overlit by its own area lamps, so the tinted acrylic washes out to pastel salmon and reads as plastic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 119, lum_p95 205, clip 0.9%, rgb median 166/105/92 (R/G 1.58, pink rather than deep red)

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area, 20.0 W/m2 at the target, 3000 K
change.to: 2 x area at 8 W/m2, moved to graze from behind and above so light passes through the acrylic and catches its polished edges rather than lighting the front faces

changes.expected: Deeper, denser red in the faces with brighter edges; the cabinet reads as thick tinted acrylic with light through it; speaker still the brightest coloured object.

changes.problem: The leather chair is a saturated orange-red that competes with the speaker as a second colour.

evidence.measured: rgb 104/67/52, delta_e 3.9 from #5A3A2A; visibly orange at full frame

change.to: dark, worn espresso or black leather, roughly #2E2420, roughness 0.45 with a creasing/grain normal map

changes.expected: The chair reads as a dark silhouette with a soft sheen; the speaker is the only saturated colour in the frame.

changes.problem: The frame is exposed slightly too bright and too neutral for a night room; the 2400 K practicals render near white.

evidence.measured: frame lum_median 57.4 (target 22-50); sconce [140,20,200,75] clip 5.1% and near neutral

change.to: white_balance_k 3800 (lets the 2400-2700 K lamps go amber), exposure -0.5 after c1 and c2, AgX look 'Punchy' off, keep 'None'

changes.expected: Warm amber practicals, warm grey concrete, frame median about 40.

changes.problem: The room is empty of life; it reads as a product on a plinth rather than a listening room in use.

evidence.measured: no glass, record, coat or book anywhere in frame

change.to: a rocks glass with a little whisky on a small blackened-steel side table by the chair, a record out of its sleeve leaning against the cabinet base of the record wall, a wool coat or throw over the chair arm, one candle in an amber votive on the floor or cabinet

changes.expected: Small warm highlights (glass, votive) in the lower left and right, a sense that someone just stood up.

changes.problem: The record wall is dark and flat; the spines read as streaks and catch no highlights.

change.setting: the record wall 3 x spot, 4.0 W, 2500 K; record-wall strip 0.3
change.to: 3 x spot 10 W, cone 40 deg grazing down the shelves; strip 0.8 under each shelf lip

changes.expected: Graded pools down each bay with readable spines and small highlights on sleeves; still clearly secondary to the speaker.

changes.problem: The level, low camera crops out the fir beams and ceiling that the brief asks for, and centres the speaker like a catalogue shot.

evidence.measured: top of frame is bare concrete; no beams visible

change.to: position about [14.3, 1.8, 1.15], target [16.3, 4.6, 1.2], 28 mm, verticals kept true (shift rather than tilt), speaker on the left-third line with the chair's back in the near foreground

changes.expected: Beams and ceiling along the top edge, the chair framing the speaker, more of the room's depth.

changes.problem: The plinth reads as raw pale pine and the concrete is slightly smooth and soft at 1:1.

evidence.measured: plinth pale, near the floor hotspot; concrete [0,0,200,120] lum_range only 98 with smoothed grain

change.setting: the fir's stain; the concrete's tone and sheen; render denoise
change.from: light natural fir, smooth concrete, denoise on at 256 samples
change.to: fir stained to an aged honey-brown matching the beams; concrete with stronger board-grain bump and tie holes, roughness 0.85; render at 512 samples with denoise prefilter 'accurate' to keep grain

changes.expected: The plinth stops pulling the eye; concrete shows formwork grain and tie holes at 1:1.

out_of_scope.request: The top panel floating above the cabinet on thin posts reads oddly and its soft highlight looks plastic
out_of_scope.why: It is part of the speaker's fixed shape; only its lighting (c2) may change.

out_of_scope.request: A deeper, more saturated Ember red in the acrylic itself
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour is fixed; c2 changes only how it is lit.
